research_insight_text_link.research_insight_description: Cyngn is researching autonomous driving systems for industrial vehicles. Work such as High-definition mapping aligns asynchronous multimodal inputs, while Modular sensor system for automated guided vehicles defines configurable sensor rail assemblies. System and method titles cover off-board-centric computation, adaptive object-based decision making, multi-channel fusion perception, motion compensation, real-time vehicle system identification, and three-dimensional object detection, together addressing perception, decision, and control layers.

overview_description.description: Cyngn's autonomous vehicle software integrates with a suite of commercially available sensors and hardware to deliver safe, scalable, and efficient self-driving vehicle solutions to industrial organizations. The company's solution is vehicle agnostic, which means heterogeneous fleets can tap into autonomy, switching easily between fully-autonomous, remotely-controlled, and manual modes. Cyngn tackles pressing issues confronted by industrial organizations in the present, including shortages in labor, expensive safety incidents, and growing consumer demands for eCommerce.

product.description: A software and hardware autonomy system that enables industrial vehicles to navigate, avoid obstacles, execute missions, and operate in autonomous or manual modes.

product.name: Teleoperations
product.description: A remote-driving service that allows trained operators to control industrial vehicles from a distance, supporting vehicle operation while reducing the need for on-site drivers.

product.description: An integration service that adds DriveMod autonomous capabilities to industrial vehicle fleets made by original equipment manufacturers.
